fixes.explanation: Yes, that's the catch. Jeremiah says to the LORD, “…for to You I have committed my cause.” He's putting it in the LORD's hands. He asks to see the LORD's vengeance, and he never says he'll take care of the plotters himself.

That's it. The people of Anathoth say, “You must not prophesy in the name of the LORD, or you will die by our hand.” They're seeking his life over it. I think that's one of the hardest things a person could hear, especially from his own hometown (Jeremiah 1:1).

Yes, horses. The words say, “…how can you compete with horses?” If men on foot already wore you out, horses are a whole other level. It's like getting winded on the walk to the mailbox and then signing up for a marathon. Bold move, friend.

Camels didn't make it into this picture. The words ask, “…how can you compete with horses?” It goes from men on foot straight to horses. Camels never even got a turn at the starting line, poor things.
No lions here, friend. The race picture says, “…how can you compete with horses?” It goes from men on foot to horses. Nobody's getting chased by a lion in this one, and honestly, my hat is relieved.
Rulers don't come up in this line. The words say your brothers, your own father's household, “…even they have betrayed you…” This one's about family.
